The first 30 natural numbers are \(1, 2, 3, \ldots, 30\), an A.P. with \(a = 1\), \(d = 1\), \(n = 30\).

\(S_n = \dfrac{n(n + 1)}{2}\)

\(S_{30} = \dfrac{30 \times 31}{2} = 15 \times 31 = 465\)

\(\therefore\) The sum is 465.

\(\therefore\) The difference is 25. (\(a\) cancels, so the first term is not needed — and note it is \(5d\), not \(d\) or \((18 - 13 + 1)d\).)

The first five multiples of 3 are \(3, 6, 9, 12, 15\).

\(3 + 6 + 9 + 12 + 15 = 45\)

By formula: \(S_5 = \dfrac{5}{2}[2 \times 3 + (5 - 1) \times 3] = \dfrac{5}{2}[6 + 12] = \dfrac{5}{2} \times 18 = 45\)

\(\therefore\) The sum is 45.
